title: An Abandoned Mine Turned Into Jade Lakes | Qinghai-Gansu Loop EP4 | China Travel Expert
description:
Stop four on the Qinghai-Gansu loop is a lake that shouldn't exist — it was an industrial mine before it became one of the most beautiful stretches of water in China.

Emerald Lake sits near Dachaidan in Qinghai, about 3,200m up and roughly 15 km² across. It formed from the flooded pits of a boron-ore mine worked by the Dachaidan Chemical Plant. The water is rich in magnesium, potassium and lithium, and those minerals paint each pool a different shade — cyan, emerald, deep blue — pool by pool. On a still morning the sky, clouds and the snow-capped Qaidam peaks land on the surface twice over. Then it's back to town for the reward at the end of the drive: a bowl of Qinghai lamb noodles.

🧭 Expert Tip: Come at dawn on a windless day for the cleanest mirror — the wind picks up by mid-morning and breaks the reflection; flat shoes and no drone-only plans, the boardwalks give the best angles.
